answers.explanation: Lower is preferred. b is the backup, used only if a doesn't answer.
Equal priorities mean the sender picks either one, which spreads the load.
Reverse the four octets and add in-addr.arpa: 7.100.51.198.in-addr.arpa.
`100.51.198.in-addr.arpa` can be handed to whoever owns 198.51.100.0/24, exactly like delegating a subdomain.
A PTR (pointer) record points from the reverse name back to a host name.
TXT records started as free text and now carry SPF, DKIM keys, and domain verification tokens.
HINFO announces a host's CPU and OS to anyone who asks. That's a gift to attackers, which is why it's almost never used.
MX combined the destination and forwarder roles into one record with priorities.
The MX gives a host name, so the sender looks up that host's A or AAAA record to get an address.
